question: An education lead is choosing a model tier to help draft feedback that will contribute to students' marks. What should she do first?
options: A) Choose the deepest tier, since anything involving students should use the strongest option.
B) Establish how the feedback will be used and what an error in it would cost a student.
C) Compare the tiers on a sample and pick whichever produces the longest and most detailed drafts.
D) Choose the fastest tier, since drafting feedback for a class is a high-volume repetitive task.
correct_answers: B) Establish how the feedback will be used and what an error in it would cost a student.
explanations: Incorrect. It may well be right, but choosing it before the quality bar is stated is a guess rather than a judgment.
Correct. The quality bar comes from the consequence of the output. Once she knows an error affects a mark, the tier decision follows from that bar rather than from cost alone.
Incorrect. Length is not the standard, and choosing on it rewards verbosity rather than accuracy.
Incorrect. Volume is only half the picture, and choosing on throughput ignores what an error here would cost.
